title: Production RAG Patterns and Latency Optimization
description: Deploy RAG in production with latency budgets, async indexing pipelines, multi-tenant isolation, and cost management strategies.

data.text: From Prototype to Production: RAG Engineering

A prototype RAG system that works fine on 100 documents breaks down at scale. Production RAG must handle: millions of documents with async indexing pipelines, sub-second query latency for interactive use, multi-tenant data isolation, cost tracking per customer, and graceful degradation when vector backends are unavailable.

data.text: The end-to-end latency of a RAG query includes: query parsing (1ms), embedding generation (10-50ms), vector search (5-50ms), cross-encoder reranking (50-200ms), prompt assembly (1ms), LLM generation (500ms-5s), streaming start (immediate). The target for interactive use is under 2 seconds total.

data.text: Async Indexing Pipeline with Durable Workflows

Documents arrive via uploads, database changes, or external sources. An async indexing pipeline: (1) receives the document, (2) chunks it with overlap, (3) generates embeddings, (4) stores vectors in the database, (5) updates search indexes. Using Durable Functions ensures exactly-once processing even if workers crash.

data.text: Multi-tenant RAG systems must prevent data leakage between customers. Approaches include: separate vector indexes per tenant, partition keys in shared indexes, and access control filters applied at query time. The filter approach is most cost-effective but requires careful implementation to prevent bypasses.

Always validate tenant access at query time, even when using partition keys. A bug in filter injection can leak data across tenants. Use defense-in-depth: database-level partitioning, application-level filtering, and audit logging.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Target sub-2-second latency for interactive RAG through embedding caching and HNSW tuning
Use Durable Functions for resilient, exactly-once document indexing pipelines
Multi-tenant isolation requires defense-in-depth: partitioning, filtering, and audit logging
Monitor the latency fingerprint: break down query time by each pipeline component
Plan re-indexing during off-peak hours as graph quality degrades with data growth
data.takeaway: Production RAG is as much about engineering (caching, partitioning, pipelines) as it is about ML. Start with a latency budget and work backward to optimize each component.
